sections.html:
Mason City is the county seat of Cerro Gordo County in north-central Iowa, about 120 miles north of Des Moines and 135 miles south of Minneapolis and Saint Paul. It sits on the Winnebago River, with Clear Lake roughly 8 miles to the west. The ZIP codes are 50401, 50402 and 50467.

The city had 27,338 residents in 2020 and has been slowly shrinking since a peak of 30,642 in 1960. With 2.07 people per household and a median age of 42.7 in 2020, a lot of homes here belong to older owners or are inherited, and many sellers are weighing a move or settling an estate.

Figures cover 2020 to 2024. A median value of $142,000 means buyers here are price-sensitive, so condition and repair costs weigh heavily on what a house will fetch.

sections.h2: Selling a Prairie School or historic house
sections.html:
Mason City has one of the largest collections of Prairie School buildings in the world. The Rock Crest and Rock Glen Historic District holds at least 32 houses and one commercial building from 1908 to 1922, and 17 of them are on the National Register of Historic Places. Designers include Walter Burley Griffin, Marion Mahony Griffin and Barry Byrne. Frank Lloyd Wright designed the Dr. G.C. Stockman House in 1908, and it was moved four blocks in 1989 to avoid demolition.

Outside those districts the city has Victorian, Craftsman, Bungalow and Mayan Revival homes. If you own a house in or near a historic district, check with the city before changing the exterior, and mention any historic status when you list or take an offer. An older, unusual house is hard to price from a standard comparable, so expect a wider range of opinions on value.

sections.h2: Selling near the river after the 2008 flood
sections.html:
In June 2008 the Winnebago River reached a record crest of 18.72 feet and overtopped the levee system. The city later ran a voluntary buyout and bought 167 properties, paid for with FEMA hazard mitigation money and HUD community development funds.

Most of the historic houses affected were in the East Park Place area, and five of the 22 individually eligible houses were relocated. East Park Historic District was added to the National Register in 2014. If your house is near the river, know its flood history and be ready for buyers to ask about flood insurance and past repairs. A February 1977 tornado and winters with an average January high of 24.2 degrees are also part of local memory, so roof and furnace condition get a close look.

sections.h2: Why people stay: parks, jobs and getting around
sections.html:
The municipal park system covers over 600 acres with more than 75 miles of trails. Healthcare is the largest employment sector, led by MercyOne North Iowa Medical Center with over 2,000 workers. Meredith Willson grew up here, and Music Man Square and the MacNider Art Museum draw visitors.

Iowa 122 and U.S. 65 serve the city, U.S. 18 bypasses it to the south, and Interstate 35 is about 8 miles west. Mason City Municipal Airport has United Airlines flights to Chicago O'Hare. A house near a park or a main road is worth a line in the listing.

sections.h2: Recording, transfer tax and property tax
sections.html:
The Cerro Gordo County Recorder is at 220 N. Washington Avenue in Mason City, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The county charges transfer tax at $1.60 per thousand with the first $500 exempt. The Recorder does not keep abstracts, and a replacement can be requested from Cerro Gordo Abstract Company at 641-423-1145. The office cannot help prepare documents, so talk to an attorney about adding or removing a name on a deed.

  • First half due September 1, delinquent October 1
  • Second half due March 1, delinquent April 1
  • Statements mailed in mid to late August
  • 1.5 percent penalty each month after the due date
  • Annual electronic tax sale on the third Monday in June

The Treasurer's number is 641-421-3127. Redemption after a tax sale costs 2 percent per month, paid with guaranteed funds. If taxes are owed when you sell, they are paid out of the sale proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: How a cash sale of a Mason City house works
sections.html:
You tell us about the house, we review the condition and the title, and if you accept an offer, a title company closes the sale with the deed and recording. No lender is involved, so no loan appraisal can delay it.

A cash buyer does not require the roof, plumbing or flood repairs to be done first, which can help with an older house. The offer reflects those repairs, so compare it with a listing's likely net after repairs, commissions and carrying costs. We do not promise a price in advance, and you owe nothing if you decline.

Before closing, gather the deed, your most recent tax statement, any mortgage payoff information and a list of known problems. The closing agent handles the paperwork and records the deed with the county.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Mason City?
faqs.a: The median value of owner-occupied homes for 2020 to 2024 is $142,000, and the median gross rent is $882.

faqs.q: When are Cerro Gordo County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. They become delinquent on October 1 and April 1, with a 1.5 percent penalty each month.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Mason City house in a historic district?
faqs.a: Yes. Check with the city about exterior rules and mention the historic status. Rock Crest and Rock Glen has 17 houses on the National Register.

faqs.q: What if I owe back taxes when I sell?
faqs.a: Unpaid taxes come out of the sale proceeds at closing. For the current payoff, call the Treasurer at 641-421-3127.
